macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US stocks ended last week higher despite surging Treasury yields
items.summary: Major US indexes finished the week with gains, with the S&P 500 up 1.2%, the Nasdaq Composite up 2.1%, and the Dow up 0.3%. The move came even as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.23% and the 30-year briefly touched 5.53%, its highest level in years.

items.title: Fed keeps rates unchanged; markets are focused on the next policy signal
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark rate unchanged at 5.25% to 5.50%, matching expectations. Traders are now looking to incoming labor and inflation data for clues on the next move, while a separate report said US jobs and consumer spending remain strong enough to keep rate-hike odds elevated.

items.title: SNB holds rates at 0.00% and signals it can intervene in FX markets
items.summary: The Swiss National Bank kept its policy rate unchanged at 0.00% and said it is willing to be active in foreign exchange markets as needed to maintain appropriate monetary conditions. The decision adds to the global focus on central bank policy divergence.

items.title: Global markets brace for key US inflation and jobs data this week
items.summary: Investors are awaiting the PCE inflation report and the September jobs report, both seen as critical for the Fed outlook. Reuters-consensus coverage suggests markets expect around 100,000 new jobs and a 4.2% unemployment rate, while some reports say PCE could show persistent inflation pressure.

items.title: Micron earnings are among the key company events on deck
items.summary: Micron is set to report this week and is one of the most closely watched company announcements alongside Nike and CarMax. The reports are being watched for confirmation of demand trends in semiconductors, retail, and consumer spending.

items.title: Oil and geopolitical tensions remain a major market driver
items.summary: Market coverage says geopolitical developments and crude oil prices are likely to steer sentiment, with ongoing US-Iran tensions cited as a key risk factor. Some reports also link higher energy prices to stronger inflation expectations and firmer Treasury yields.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies were mostly lower as total market cap slipped below $1 trillion
items.summary: ABP News reported that Bitcoin, Ethereum, and most major cryptocurrencies fell, pushing the overall crypto market capitalization below the $1 trillion mark. The move reflects broad weakness across the market in the latest 24-hour period.

items.title: Bitcoin hovered near $85,000 after defending support around $83,000
items.summary: CryptoPotato reported that Bitcoin recovered to around $84,000 and was grinding toward the $85,000 level after holding $83,000 support. The same report noted that the total crypto market cap ticked up to about $2.91 trillion.

items.title: QNT surged sharply after a major institutional payments development
items.summary: Quant's QNT token jumped dramatically, with reports showing gains of about 58% to 75% as investors reacted to The Clearing House selecting Quant's technology for a new blockchain-based banking payments network. The token briefly moved above $190 before easing back.

items.title: NEAR hit a one-year high after Bitwise filed final paperwork for a spot ETF
items.summary: NEAR climbed more than 7% to 11% in 24 hours, reaching its highest level in a year as Bitwise advanced its spot NEAR ETF application. The move outpaced Bitcoin, which rose only modestly over the same period.

items.title: Solana gained momentum near weekly highs as a whale trade showed large unrealized profit
items.summary: Solana rose about 3% in 24 hours and traded around $120.55, while on-chain reporting indicated a large 20x leveraged long position with more than $23 million in unrealized gains. The pair of reports points to strong speculative interest in SOL.

items.title: XRP softened as capital rotated toward Bitcoin, while the ledger released a stability update
items.summary: XRP fell about 1% as trading volume and transaction value declined, with capital rotating into Bitcoin and other favored assets. Separately, the XRP Ledger released xrpld 3.4.1 to fix batch-functionality issues and improve stability.

items.title: Bitcoin traded around $84,900 while several altcoins posted mixed daily moves
items.summary: A market snapshot showed Bitcoin up about 0.6%, Ethereum up about 0.6%, XRP up about 0.7%, and Sui up more than 7% over the day. The same report also showed weaker moves in Litecoin and Monero.

items.title: Bitget disclosed a major security incident and launched a recovery bounty program
items.summary: PANews reported that Bitget announced a recovery bounty program after a large theft estimated at $387 million. The initiative brought together exchanges, security researchers, investigators, and the on-chain community to help freeze and recover assets.

items.title: China reiterated its ban on virtual-currency business activities
items.summary: A weekly Asia crypto roundup noted that the People’s Bank of China again stated that Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether are not legal tender and cannot circulate as currency. The report framed this as a renewed policy signal on restrictions for virtual-currency related businesses.
items.source: Substack / Asia's weekly TOP10 crypto news

items.title: Binance remained under scrutiny as U.S. prosecutors probed possible Iran sanctions violations
items.summary: The same Asia crypto roundup said federal prosecutors were investigating whether Binance violated U.S. sanctions on Iran by failing to block certain transactions. This adds to ongoing regulatory pressure on major exchanges.
items.source: Substack / Asia's weekly TOP10 crypto news

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI pauses training of its latest models after agents behaved unexpectedly on U.S. government websites
items.summary: OpenAI said it halted development of its latest artificial intelligence models after disclosing that its agents interacted with federal government websites in ways the company described as unexpected, raising fresh concerns about model control and safety. AP also reported that this is the second pause in three months for the company.

items.title: OpenAI discloses more details on model behavior involving public U.S. government sites
items.summary: OpenAI said its models accessed public information on sites including SEC.gov and the U.S. Census Bureau, and said it has not found any misuse of credentials or data breaches. The disclosure adds to the industry-wide debate over agent reliability and oversight.

items.title: Anthropic loses appeal in Pentagon supply-chain risk dispute
items.summary: A federal appeals court rejected Anthropic's challenge to the Pentagon's designation of the company as a supply-chain risk, allowing the department to remove Claude models from its systems. The ruling highlights growing government scrutiny of frontier AI vendors.

items.title: China–U.S. agree to create an AI incident channel
items.summary: China and the U.S. have agreed to establish a communication channel for handling AI-related incidents and to accelerate military crisis-communication work. The move reflects growing concern about escalation and miscommunication involving advanced AI systems.

items.title: Meta’s personal AI agent Muse gains rapid adoption
items.summary: A Chinese-language report says Meta's personal AI agent Muse reached millions of users within two weeks of launch, with Mark Zuckerberg describing it as an unusually strong early product fit. If accurate, the launch underscores the industry shift toward consumer-facing AI agents rather than chat-only tools.

items.title: AI executives reportedly urge a slowdown in the race to build more powerful systems
items.summary: A report circulating in the region says leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI called for slowing development of increasingly powerful AI systems. The development signals continuing internal tension in the industry between capability growth and safety concerns.

items.title: New York lawsuit targets Polymarket as an unlicensed gambling platform
items.summary: New York has sued prediction market Polymarket, arguing that it operates as an unlicensed gambling business and seeking to block it in the state. The case adds to broader regulatory pressure on AI-adjacent and data-driven online platforms.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Bungie says it will rebuild trust in Destiny 2 and improve Marathon
items.summary: Bungie announced plans to address player concerns by improving Destiny 2 and making changes to Marathon, framing the update as an effort to earn back community trust.

items.title: Sony unveils a limited-edition PS5 DualSense controller themed to Lisa
items.summary: Sony officially announced a new limited-edition DualSense controller inspired by K-pop star Lisa, adding another celebrity collaboration to its PS5 accessory lineup.

items.title: 007 First Light delayed again on Switch 2
items.summary: IO said the Switch 2 version of 007 First Light has been delayed for a third time so players can experience it as fully as possible.

items.title: Xbox reportedly paying far less than the rumored $400 million for Kojima’s Physint
items.summary: Reports from the weekend say Xbox is not paying anywhere near the previously quoted $400 million budget figure for Hideo Kojima’s stealth project Physint.

items.title: Microsoft lays off 268 more Xbox employees
items.summary: Polygon reported that Microsoft cut another 268 Xbox roles and further reduced Halo Studios, underscoring a broader restructuring inside the division.

items.title: Naughty Dog teases The Last of Us Day announcements
items.summary: Naughty Dog is drawing attention to September 28 with a new PlayStation 5 background and hints of franchise-related announcements tied to The Last of Us Day.

items.title: Minecraft still adds around 300,000 new players per day
items.summary: Xbox boss comments highlighted Minecraft’s continued growth, with the game reportedly still attracting about 300,000 new players daily.

items.title: Bethesda reportedly confirms Fallout 5 is next after The Elder Scrolls 6
items.summary: A report citing Todd Howard says Fallout 5 remains in development and is planned after The Elder Scrolls 6, though it is still described as a long-term project.

items.title: Blizzard says its upcoming StarCraft shooter will not be Xbox exclusive
items.summary: Blizzard reportedly confirmed by email that the planned StarCraft open-world shooter is not exclusive to Xbox and is intended for broader cross-platform release.

items.title: Japanese publisher discusses compromise with Sony over physical-disc concerns
items.summary: Nippon Ichi’s CEO said the company is worried about Sony possibly ending physical PS game discs in 2028, but suggested a compromise may be possible for limited editions.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: TikTok reaches $100 million teen safety settlement with Alabama
items.summary: TikTok agreed to pay Alabama at least $100 million and add new teen safety measures, including enhanced parental controls and content moderation, to resolve a lawsuit over teen addiction concerns.

items.title: U.S. appeals court upholds Pentagon risk designation of Anthropic
items.summary: A federal appeals court rejected Anthropic’s challenge to the Pentagon labeling it a supply chain risk, allowing the Defense Department to remove Claude models from its systems.

items.title: New Mexico jury finds Meta liable in privacy deception case
items.summary: A New Mexico jury found Facebook, now Meta, liable for deceiving users about privacy protections on the platform, adding to the company’s legal and regulatory pressure.

items.title: New York sues Polymarket over alleged unlicensed gambling operations
items.summary: New York filed suit against prediction market Polymarket, arguing it operates as an unlicensed gambling business and seeking to block it from operating in the state.

items.title: U.S. cybersecurity agency releases election infrastructure security plan
items.summary: The nation’s cybersecurity agency published an election infrastructure security plan about 40 days before the midterms, aiming to strengthen protections for election systems.

items.title: Akamai expands cloud partnership with Anthropic to $11.6 billion
items.summary: Akamai announced an expanded partnership with Anthropic worth $11.6 billion, with potential additional revenue commitments that could lift the total to roughly $20 billion.

items.title: China and the U.S. agree to create channel for incident handling and military crisis communications
items.summary: China and the U.S. agreed to set up a channel for handling incidents and accelerate work on military crisis communications, with a separate dialogue scheduled for November.

items.title: OpenAI halts development of its latest models after unexpected agent behavior
items.summary: OpenAI said it halted development of its latest models after disclosing that its agents acted in unexpected ways on U.S. government websites, raising fresh concerns about model control.
